notes.meaning: Deep darkness covered the entire area from noon until three o'clock in the afternoon. This was not a normal solar eclipse, because the Passover happened during a full moon. The midday blackness showed God's judgment and reflected the heavy sorrow of Christ's suffering.

Jesus cried out loudly to God in Aramaic, quoting the first words of Psalm 22. In this terrible hour, He carried the heavy burden of human sin and felt cut off from the comforting presence of His Father. Even in this deepest pain, calling Him 'My God' showed that He never stopped trusting the Father.

differ.view: Jesus experienced a real, terrible separation from the Father as He bore God's full wrath and punishment against sin in our place.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern teachers claim Jesus suffered spiritual death, fell completely under Satan's power in hell, and needed to be born again before rising.

notes.meaning: Some people standing by heard His cry and thought He was calling for the ancient prophet Elijah. The Hebrew word for 'My God' sounded very much like Elijah's name. They knew the popular Jewish belief that Elijah would come back to rescue people in distress.

A bystander quickly soaked a sponge in sour wine, placed it on a long stalk, and lifted it to Jesus' mouth. Crucifixion caused terrible thirst, and this cheap soldier's drink was given to moisten His lips.

Other people told the man to step back and leave Jesus alone. They wanted to wait and see if Elijah would really appear to rescue Him from the cross. Their words treated Jesus' dying agony like a spectacle to watch.

Jesus shouted once more with a loud voice and released His spirit. His death was not an accident or mere physical exhaustion. He gave up His life willingly as a free choice once His saving work was finished.

The thick curtain inside the temple tore straight down the middle from the top to the bottom, and an earthquake split giant rocks open. God tore the curtain Himself to show that the barrier between holy God and sinful humanity was gone. Through Jesus' death, everyone can now come directly into God's presence.

differ.view: The torn curtain showed that the ceremonial rules and temple sacrifices of Moses were permanently finished, opening heaven to all believers as a royal priesthood.
The split curtain proved that the dividing wall between Jewish people and Gentiles was broken down, giving the whole world equal access to God's mercy.

notes.meaning: The earthquake cracked graves open, and many godly believers were raised to life. After Jesus rose from the dead, these saints came out of the tombs, walked into Jerusalem, and were seen by many people. Christ's victory over the grave proved that He conquered death and will one day raise all who trust in Him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars consider this event to be a symbolic story rather than a literal historical event because it appears only in Matthew's Gospel.

notes.meaning: The Roman commander and the soldiers guarding the cross were filled with terror when they felt the earthquake and saw how Jesus died. These Gentile soldiers recognized God's hand at work and confessed that Jesus was truly the Son of God.

A large group of women who had traveled with Jesus from Galilee to care for His needs watched everything from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of James and John. While most of the male disciples had run away in fear, these women stayed loyal and stayed near.

As evening came, a wealthy disciple named Joseph from the town of Arimathea arrived. He went directly to Pilate and asked permission to take Jesus' body down for burial. Pilate agreed, which kept Jesus from being thrown into a dishonorable common grave for criminals.

Joseph took the body, wrapped it carefully in clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own unused tomb carved out of solid rock. He then rolled a huge stone over the doorway and left. This loving act gave Jesus an honorable burial and fulfilled the ancient prophecy that the Messiah would be with the rich in His death.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary stayed behind and sat down across from the tomb. They kept watch through their grief to see exactly where Jesus was laid so they could return after the Sabbath.

The next day, which was the Sabbath day of rest, the leading priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate. Even on their sacred day, their fear of Jesus drove them to do business with the Roman governor.

The rulers warned Pilate that Jesus had claimed He would rise from the dead after three days. They asked for soldiers to guard the tomb until the third day so His followers could not steal the body and trick the public. They feared that a fake resurrection story would be harder to stop than His original teachings.
Pilate granted their request and gave them permission to place a guard at the tomb. He told them to go and make the grave as secure as they possibly could.

The leaders sealed the giant stone with an official mark and stationed soldiers outside the tomb. Their careful security measures backfired, because the sealed stone and armed guards provided undeniable proof that Jesus really rose from the dead.
